I played this on pc as a kid in the 90s. My parents usually only allowed educational games and this came in a pack of Broderbund titles. My sisters and I loved its goofy style and puzzles. It looked like a little kid game, but the puzzles get quite complicated, especially if you raise the challenge level. I was not disappointed playing it again. I admit there is a bit of nostalgia bias on my end, but this was really fun to buy and play with my kids. At the time of this writing, I have a 1st grader and a 7th grader who both like puzzle/logic games. The object of the game is to get all of the Zoombinis safely from their Isle that was taken over by a group of mean creatures and get them to a new home. The graphics still hold up well and the characters and voices are as fun as I remember. My 1st grader needs help even on the lowest setting, but we set up her own profile and play together. She loves creating the Zoombinis and trying to do whatever she can as we go through the different challenges on the journey. My 7th grader and I were enjoying figuring out the challenges on our first few rounds while laughing at the noises, voices, etc... This isn't a game that is going to keep a teen or adult busy all day, but if you like something to play occasionally that is a simple format, yet still challenges your logic muscles because you can raise the challenge level, then hopefully you enjoy this one. It is repetitive to a degree because you're doing the journey as many times as it takes you to get all the Zoombinis from the Isle to the new Zoombiniville, but each time you depart will be different based on the group of Zoombinis you're guiding. No boss battles or fighting, just different logic puzzles to solve to make your way through. Sometimes you'll lose a few in the challenges and they go back to the last camp and you'll have to try again another time.

A wonderful remake of Logical Journey of the Zoombinis from 1996. The visuals are redone in hand-drawn HD - the backgrounds are brighter compared to the original game and Zoombini assets have been completely remade, making for increased visual clarity compared to the original. NPCs retain their sprites and animations and have just been touched up, they are directly traced over in HD. Audio is the same as the original game. As of February 22 2026, Zoombinis retain their original voices but not their movement sounds, which are absent. The number of required Zoombinis to get to the end has been reduced by about 200, meaning you don't have to replay the game as many times as in the original. The game's pace is faster than the original version, making for shorter waiting periods, but also causes voice lines to overlap (this is especially noticeable in Stone Cold Caves and unavoidable during the intro to Hotel Dimensia). The aspect ratio of the game is wider than the original, which causes some NPC assets to get cut off at a certain part of the screen (some of Captain Cajun's animations and most of Ulla Instantaneous's animations).
There is currently a bug that can occur when placing a click-and-drag object such as a Zoombini or a toad where the asset will get stuck and you'll be unable to move it. This can and will make puzzles unbeatable. Please fix the bug.

This is exactly the same as the original Logical Journey of the Zoombinis, but brought into Steam.

I give this a positive review because of the nostalgic value the game holds.

Overall, the game is great because it's exactly the same gameplay from when you played the original logical journey game. It's full of a variety of puzzles for you to solve. Everything from the Pizza troll game, to the mudball game, the mirror game, and of course the wretched frog game. It's still the same game you played so long ago.

The problem is that the whole is the same art style with the exception of the zoombinis themselves. In the original game, the same artist drew up the zoombinis so the entire atmosphere fit together beautifully. However, for this version, since only the zoombinis are stylized in a modern way, the art style no longer fits the overall atmosphere of the game. It's somewhat off putting.

Nonetheless, if you want to play a series of different puzzles then the game certainly still contains the charm from the original game.

As an adult I used to think about my time as a child and wondered if that game I used to play on the computers at the school actually existed.  I mean, a game about logic where you had to get a bunch of various blue creatures to a magical land, it sounded insane.
Imagine my surprise when I found it was actually real, and my mind was blown!  It is a child game for sure and I understand why I liked it.  It was a puzzle that I could almost grasp, but was slightly out of reach because my brain was far from fully developed.  It was fun to introduce it to my own children who enjoy the same things as me and see them try and logic things out.  I do admit there were a few games that I didn't understand at first, but I believe it is more because the instructions were not clear, not because I couldn't figure it out at first.  I am please to say that I got all the Zoombinies to their final location with all the buildings built.  Then my kids deleted my game, so...that sucked.  Still, it is a kids game so I will leave it to them.  
The only thing I don't like is that there is some dead space between things when it should move on.  A few of the puzzles, the mirror one comes to mind, where you have to manually reset the puzzle every time is annoying.  Also, don't get me started on the frogs puzzle, that is just a time waster.  It is also easy to cheese, you could just make all your Zoombinis the same and it would be the easiest thing you ever played, also you would be lame to make one Zoombini clone! The Fleens would also screw you over.
I do wonder if there are more games with the Zoombinis, it seems like there are things that should be heavier used in the game and hints at a broader world but are just not present.  It makes me think that there are more games, if anybody knows about them you should let me know.
As a kid I would probably rate this an 8/10, but as an adult I think it falls to a 6/10.  Not really built for adults, gameplay gets stale, but I could see as a kid how I cared for every single one of my weird little Zoombinies and wanted to seem them all succeed and reach the promised Zoombiniville!  When I did it as an adult I did feel accomplished, but wouldn't do it again.  Still, worth the price it costs.

Zoombinis is a total blast from the past and a great way to relive a childhood favorite. The logic puzzles, quirky animations, and charming characters are just as fun and brain-teasing as I remember. It’s awesome to see it available on Steam so a new generation (and nostalgic fans like me) can enjoy it again.

That said—this is literally a direct port of the classic game. No major updates, no visual overhaul, no new puzzles or features. While the gameplay still holds up, it feels like a missed opportunity to modernize it just a bit with refreshed visuals, smoother movement, or even new puzzle paths to surprise returning players.

Still, for fans of classic edutainment games, this is a solid way to revisit the world of the Zoombinis.

Final Thoughts:
🧠 Yes, I recommend it, especially for those looking to scratch that nostalgia itch. Just don’t expect anything new beyond the original game.

🌀 7.5/10 – Classic charm intact, but could use a magical remaster
